meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-10 | Time: 16:00-16:48 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Redwood CSM); Maya Thompson, Evan Cruz, Dr. Luis Ortega (HavenHealth)
transcript: 00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan li from redwood inference, i'll hand over to priya for the tech agenda, but quick intro, we're here to scope the poc for private networking and data residency for your clinical NLP workload, yeah 00:15 Priya: thanks jordan, hi maya, evan, luis, quick run of what we want to cover: network options (vpc peering vs private link), region choices, egress restrictions, success criteria like p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts, throughput targets, and bench plan, also we'll talk sizing — tokens per day and model families 00:35 Maya: sounds good, today our main constraint is that PHI can't leave eu-west-1 and we need all logs to be stored on-prem or in our encrypted s3 in eu-west-1, also evan has some specifics on egress policies 00:50 Evan: yeah in our environment any egress to public internet is blocked by default. we can allow controlled private endpoints. we prefer PrivateLink but would consider VPC peering if the routing is simpler and we can avoid extra hops that add latency, also we need TLS and customer-managed KMS at rest for any cached artifacts 01:10 Priya: ok noted, private link commonly called PrivateLink or privatelink sometimes in docs, it's the aws interface endpoint approach — pros: no cross-account route table changes, works over aws backbone, and you can keep traffic inside region; cons: some protocols need extra configuration and you pay for interface endpoints and data processing 01:30 Jordan: and vpc peering is a layer 3 peering between our infra vpc and your vpc — works very well for throughput, very low latency typically, but requires route table updates and security controls, and for cross-account peering you also have to manage route set up 01:45 Dr. Luis: latency is a big deal for our clinical chat assistant — we need sub-500ms response for prompts under 512 tokens on average, and p95 ideally under 800ms for longer batches, but cost tradeoffs matter too 02:05 Priya: good to have target numbers, for the poc we'll test with a 512-token and 1,024-token mix — we'll capture p50/p95 and per-token cost; recommended starting model is a 13B open model quantized to int8 equivalent performance in redwood private, that maps to N model family in our catalog 02:25 Jordan: can i clarify the data flows? so requests originate inside your vpc, hit the redwood private endpoint (via peering or privatelink), redwood runs inference in your chosen region, and responses flow back — we can also support an on-prem private control plane if needed for audits 02:40 Maya: we need to define where logs and KV cache live — can they be kept in our s3 or in a customer-controlled redis in our vpc? 02:55 Priya: yes, for the poc we can keep KV cache in your vpc (customer redis) behind security groups; logs can be delivered to your s3 with SSE-KMS; we also support audit logging to your SIEM via syslog / splunk forwarder 03:15 Evan: about egress: we can't allow any calls to public model registries, so model artifacts must be pre-provisioned and pulled from an approved bucket or shipped via airgap if necessary 03:30 Jordan: that's fine — for redwood private we can pre-stage the model bits into your account's s3 (we do a signed transfer) and then the runtime only reads from that s3; no external registry calls during inference 03:45 Dr. Luis: benchmark volume: we expect 50k inference requests per day initially, average 400 tokens per request, bursty during business hours up to 200rps for short bursts — can you size for that? 04:05 Priya: yes, initial sizing for 50k req/day at 400 tokens is about 20M tokens/day. with batching and kv cache we can reduce effective compute. for a 13B quantized model, rough estimate is 30-40 inf tokens per second per GPU depending on sequence length; we'll propose GPU counts in the benchmark doc 04:30 Jordan: actionables from us will include recommended node counts, autoscale policy, and a cost projection for hosted vs dedicated vs private modes, but since you require data residency private is the clear path 04:45 Maya: region question: we want eu-west-1 only initially; later we might expand to ca-central-1, but pilot must remain eu-west-1 and all backups must stay in-region 05:00 Priya: noted; PrivateLink works per region — interface endpoints are regional so peering or privatelink must be in eu-west-1. if you later expand we can set up inter-region routing but that's a separate project 05:15 Evan: one more security ask: SAML SSO for admin console, RBAC with least privilege, and i want to see proof of SOC two compliance and a pen test report 05:30 Jordan: we'll share SOC 2 report and a recent pen test summary, and we support SAML SSO and RBAC — i'll include the docs in the follow-up 05:45 Dr. Luis: for success criteria let's be explicit: 1) functional: inference outputs match baseline quality metrics on our eval prompts (F1/precision/recall targets), 2) performance: p95 latency < 800ms for mixed sequences, 3) reliability: 99.9% availability during business hours for the pilot, 4) security: all data and logs remain in eu-west-1 and encrypted with customer KMS 06:15 Priya: that aligns with our POC templates — we'll run a 2-week benchmark window: week 1 dry run and week 2 production-like traffic. we'll instrument with traces and token-level cost metrics so you can evaluate unit economics 06:35 Jordan: timeline: we'd like to kickoff prep in mid-december but realistically operational start for the POC in early jan, propose pilot window jan 6 - jan 20 06:50 Maya: jan 6 works for us if we can get the network diagram and the pre-stage model artifacts in advance 07:05 Priya: on benchmarking specifics — we'll request a sample dataset of 5k prompts (anonymized) and a script to replay traffic with adjustable qps and seq len; we'll run experiments with different batch sizes (1, 4, 8) and measure p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec plus cost per 1k tokens 07:30 Evan: regarding egress accounting, we need a clear chart of what flows leave our vpc. any calls to telemetry or feature flags must be optional and allow an on-prem collector; we will not allow telemetry that sends PHI 07:50 Jordan: agreed, telemetry can be configured to point at your splunk or to be disabled; we will not transmit PHI in telemetry by default, and we'll sign an addendum for logging policy 08:05 Dr. Luis: any gotchas with kv cache? how long does it persist and is it inside our vpc? 08:20 Priya: kv cache TTL is configurable; for the poc we'll set short TTLs to simulate typical chat sessions and keep cache in your redis inside the vpc, so no external storage of session state 08:35 Maya: cost — we need a rough cost projection to justify the pilot; can you estimate per-million-token cost and a delta between privatelink and peering? 08:50 Jordan: very roughly, network egress via PrivateLink will incur interface endpoint charges and data processing fees (~$0.01-$0.02 per GB depending on region) whereas peering has no interface fees but you manage the route and CT ingress/egress costs are often lower; biggest delta will be management effort vs small network fees — we'll include a cost sensitivity table 09:10 Priya: one important bench detail: measure cold-start vs warm requests separately, because model cold starts (new KV cache) can add 200-800ms depending on model and instance; we'll include warm-only and mixed windows 09:30 Evan: for compliance: if we're using customer-managed CMKs, we want key access logs and an ability to rotate keys without downtime 09:45 Jordan: supported — we integrate with your KMS and we can support key rotation with a short handoff window; we'll document the process 10:00 Priya: summary of technical deliverables from redwood: 1) VPC peering vs PrivateLink pros/cons + diagram, 2) benchmark config + test scripts, 3) recommended infra sizing and autoscale policy, 4) security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, SAML docs), 5) cost projection, all by 2026-12-15 10:30 Maya: looks good, after we review we'll confirm account ids and provide anonymized prompts 10:45 Jordan: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the network walkthrough and a proposed pilot kickoff on 2027-01-06, thanks everyone 10:55 Evan: thanks, bye 11:00 End of recording (note: auto timestamps sometimes drift)
